title: E-Readers With Big, Adjustable Type: Kobo Clara BW, NOOK GlowLight 4 and Kobo Libra Colour Compared
subtitle: Three e-readers that can make reading easier, compared on screen size, waterproofing, listed features and price, based on product pages and published reviews.
excerpt: If small print has started getting in the way of a good book, an e-reader lets you make the words bigger. Here is how three models compare on paper, and what to check before you give one as a gift.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: Many lifelong readers reach a point where paperback print feels too small and the lamp is never quite bright enough. A thick hardcover can also get heavy in the hands.

An e-reader is a small device built only for reading books. With a few taps you can usually make the letters larger, and many have a built-in light. For an avid reader, or for an adult child shopping for a holiday gift, it can be a practical way to keep the reading going. A note on sources: everything below comes from the makers' product pages and published reviews. It is a comparison of listed features, not a hands-on test.

The Kobo models here use a screen called E Ink, and Kobo describes the Libra Colour as glare-free. Barnes & Noble describes the NOOK GlowLight 4 screen as glare-free and scratch-resistant. All three have a built-in front light you can adjust. The NOOK also has a Night Mode with a warm sepia tone.

Books are bought as digital files and stored on the device. One thing to know up front: e-reader makers typically sell ebooks only through their own store, according to NBC News Select. Books bought for a Kindle will not move over to a Kobo or a NOOK.
"The most important feature of an e-reader is its screen," says Mantha, in an NBC News Select shopping guide.

That matters even more in large type. Bigger letters mean fewer words fit on each page. As a general rule of thumb, a 7-inch screen will show more text at a large size than a 6-inch screen, so you may turn pages less often. The Clara BW and GlowLight 4 have 6-inch screens, and the Libra Colour has a 7-inch screen.

items: Font size range: This is the main question. Only Kobo's page for the Libra Colour confirms font size and margin controls. The Clara BW and GlowLight 4 pages do not state their font range, so check the font menu before you buy, or ask the seller how large the text goes.
Screen size: A 6-inch screen shows fewer words per page in large print. A 7-inch screen leaves more room.
Page-turn buttons: Some people find buttons easier than swiping. Kobo's page confirms them on the Libra Colour. Check the product page for the model you are considering.
Light: Look for an adjustable front light. The Clara BW lists blue light control, and the NOOK lists a warm Night Mode.
Waterproofing: Handy for anyone who reads in the bath or by the pool. The Clara BW and Libra Colour are listed as waterproof. The GlowLight 4 is not.
Your existing library: Kindle books will not transfer to a Kobo or NOOK.
Extra costs: Covers, a stylus or a subscription can add to the price. Kobo Plus is a subscription service, and its price was not verified here. Ask about the return policy, too.

sections.content: NBC News Select named the Kobo Clara BW its best overall Kindle alternative. It called a simple e-reader like it more than enough for reading ebooks. It also chose the Kobo Libra Colour as its best color pick. That guide is undated in the notes, so do not assume those picks are current.

Tom's Guide measured about a month of battery life on the NOOK GlowLight 4. Its drawbacks included a thinner feature list than rival devices and what the reviewer called a miserable experience with sideloading, which means loading books from outside the NOOK store. That review is also undated in the notes.

Digitec, a Swiss tech outlet, said the Libra Colour's colors look very pale because of E Ink, and that the 7-inch size makes comics hard to read. That review is older, from roughly early 2024. Families may also want to look at Amazon's Kindle, which reviewers rank highly, though its prices and font details are not covered here.
Setting it up and reading comfortably

Each of these devices needs Wi-Fi, an account and a sign-in to the bookstore before the first book arrives. If you are giving one as a gift, consider setting it up ahead of time, charging it, and loading a favorite title or two so it is ready to read out of the box.
Then sit down together and find the text settings. Try a few font sizes and styles, adjust the margins if the device allows it, and turn the brightness up or down until the page looks comfortable.

An e-reader is a reading device only. It does not do video calls or run everyday apps. It is also not a fix for serious vision loss. Anyone with vision concerns should talk with their eye doctor before relying on any e-reader's text settings. The doctor may suggest magnifiers or devices that read text aloud.
sections.label: Good to Know

sections.content: For a reader who loves a good book but is tired of squinting, one of these may be worth a look. Check the font menu, think about screen size and price, and set it up with care. Then the only thing left to choose is what to read first.

products.price: $159.99 (list price on Kobo's page, November 2026; check current price)
products.blurb: A waterproof 6-inch e-reader with an adjustable front light and blue light control, and 16GB of storage. Kobo's page does not state its font size range. The Clara Colour/BW SleepCover is sold separately for $29.99.

products.name: NOOK GlowLight 4
products.price: $149.99 (list price on Barnes & Noble's page, November 2026; check current price)
products.blurb: Suits Barnes & Noble shoppers who want a 6-inch glare-free screen, a warm Night Mode and 32GB of storage. It is not waterproof, and its font size range is not stated on the product page.

products.name: Kobo Libra Colour
products.price: $259.99 at Best Buy (November 2026; check current price). Best Buy also shows an 8-payment option starting at $32.50, but its terms are not given.
products.blurb: Suits readers who want a larger 7-inch color screen. Kobo's page lists page-turn buttons and adjustable font size, margins and style, and the device is waterproof. A stylus is sold separately, and Kobo's own page shows no price.
